fr: Je n'ai pas de stylo.
en: I don't have a pen.
ipa: /ʒə nɛ pa də sti.lo/
notes: The elided n' before ai must be written even though it almost disappears in fast speech.

fr: Elle ne mange pas de viande.
en: She doesn't eat meat.
ipa: /ɛl nə mɑ̃ʒ pa də vjɑ̃d/
notes: The ne before mange is barely audible but still required in writing.

fr: Nous n'avons pas faim.
en: We are not hungry.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ pa fɛ̃/
notes: Faim ends in a nasal vowel sound with no audible consonant, so listen for the nasal quality rather than a final letter.

fr: Tu ne parles pas anglais.
en: You don't speak English.
ipa: /ty nə paʁl pa ɑ̃.ɡlɛ/
notes: The final s of parles is silent, so do not skip writing it just because you cannot hear it.

fr: Il n'aime pas le café.
en: He doesn't like coffee.
ipa: /il nɛm pa lə ka.fe/
notes: N'aime elides ne before the vowel of aime, so remember the apostrophe when writing.

fr: Je ne bois jamais de vin.
en: I never drink wine.
ipa: /ʒə nə bwa ʒa.mɛ də vɛ̃/
notes: Vin ends in a nasal vowel that sounds close to other nasal words, so listen carefully to the vowel quality.

fr: Elle ne sort jamais le soir.
en: She never goes out in the evening.
ipa: /ɛl nə sɔʁ ʒa.mɛ lə swaʁ/
notes: The final t of sort is silent, so don't drop it from the spelling.

fr: Nous ne voyons personne ici.
en: We don't see anyone here.
ipa: /nu nə vwa.jɔ̃ pɛʁ.sɔn i.si/
notes: Personne is spelled with a double n even though it is pronounced with a single nasal sound.

fr: Il ne fait rien aujourd'hui.
en: He isn't doing anything today.
ipa: /il nə fɛ ʁjɛ̃ o.ʒuʁ.dɥi/
notes: The n of rien links smoothly into aujourd'hui, so listen for the liaison sound before writing the two separate words.

fr: Je n'ai plus de pain.
en: I don't have any bread left.
ipa: /ʒə nɛ ply də pɛ̃/
notes: Pain sounds identical to pin, so rely on context to know which spelling is correct.

fr: Tu n'as rien dans ton sac.
en: You don't have anything in your bag.
ipa: /ty na ʁjɛ̃ dɑ̃ tɔ̃ sak/
notes: Ton must agree with the masculine noun sac, so do not write ta by mistake.

fr: Elle n'a qu'un frère.
en: She only has one brother.
ipa: /ɛl na kœ̃ fʁɛʁ/
notes: Que elides to qu' before the vowel sound of un, so the apostrophe is required.

fr: Il ne mange que des légumes.
en: He only eats vegetables.
ipa: /il nə mɑ̃ʒ kə de le.ɡym/
notes: The unstressed que is often swallowed in speech, so listen for the light schwa sound before writing it.

fr: Nous n'avons aucune idée.
en: We have no idea.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ o.kyn i.de/
notes: Aucune must agree in the feminine with idée, not the masculine aucun.

fr: Je ne vois aucun problème.
en: I don't see any problem.
ipa: /ʒə nə vwa o.kœ̃ pʁɔ.blɛm/
notes: Aucun is spelled with au, not o, even though the sound is short.

fr: Elle ne parle ni français ni anglais.
en: She speaks neither French nor English.
ipa: /ɛl nə paʁl ni fʁɑ̃.sɛ ni ɑ̃.ɡlɛ/
notes: Français needs its cedilla under the c to keep the soft s sound.

fr: Il n'y a personne à la maison.
en: There is nobody at home.
ipa: /il nja pɛʁ.sɔn a la mɛ.zɔ̃/
notes: N'y a elides ne before y, so three short sounds collapse into one quick syllable that must still be written out fully.

fr: Je ne travaille jamais le dimanche.
en: I never work on Sundays.
ipa: /ʒə nə tʁa.vaj ʒa.mɛ lə di.mɑ̃ʃ/
notes: The ne before travaille is easy to drop in fast speech but is still required in writing.

fr: Tu n'écoutes pas la radio.
en: You don't listen to the radio.
ipa: /ty ne.kut pa la ʁa.djo/
notes: N'écoutes elides ne before the vowel of écoutes, so keep the apostrophe when writing.

fr: Nous ne sommes jamais en retard.
en: We are never late.
ipa: /nu nə sɔm ʒa.mɛ ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ/
notes: En retard uses a nasal vowel sound rather than a pronounced n, so listen for the nasal quality.

fr: Elle n'habite plus ici.
en: She doesn't live here anymore.
ipa: /ɛl na.bit ply i.si/
notes: The h in habite is silent, so the elision n' still applies as if the word began with a vowel.

fr: Elle ne boit que de l'eau glacée.
en: She only drinks ice-cold water.
ipa: /ɛl nə bwa kə də lo ɡla.se/
notes: De l'eau contains two elisions in a row, so both apostrophes must be written even though the sounds blend together.

fr: Je n'ai pas fini mes devoirs hier soir.
en: I didn't finish my homework last night.
ipa: /ʒə nɛ pa fi.ni me də.vwaʁ jɛʁ swaʁ/
notes: In passé composé negation, pas goes right after the auxiliary ai, before the past participle fini.

fr: Elle n'a pas répondu à mon message.
en: She didn't reply to my message.
ipa: /ɛl na pa ʁe.pɔ̃.dy a mɔ̃ me.saʒ/
notes: Répondu à uses the preposition à, easily confused with the verb form a in this same sentence.

fr: Nous n'avons pas visité le musée samedi.
en: We didn't visit the museum on Saturday.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ pa vi.zi.te lə my.ze sam.di/
notes: The negation wraps around avons, not around visité, so pas comes before the past participle.

fr: Il n'a pas pris son parapluie ce matin.
en: He didn't take his umbrella this morning.
ipa: /il na pa pʁi sɔ̃ pa.ʁa.plɥi sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: Pris is an irregular past participle that keeps a silent final s, so don't forget it in spelling.

fr: Tu n'as pas fermé la porte à clé.
en: You didn't lock the door.
ipa: /ty na pa fɛʁ.me la pɔʁt a kle/
notes: À clé uses the preposition à, not the verb a, even though both sound identical.

fr: Ils n'ont pas payé la facture ce mois-ci.
en: They didn't pay the bill this month.
ipa: /il nɔ̃ pa pe.je la fak.tyʁ sə mwa.si/
notes: Ont sounds exactly like on, so context alone tells you which spelling to use here.

fr: Vous n'avez pas compris la question.
en: You didn't understand the question.
ipa: /vu na.ve pa kɔ̃.pʁi la kɛs.tjɔ̃/
notes: Compris ends in a silent s that must still appear in writing.

fr: Elle n'est pas venue à la réunion.
en: She didn't come to the meeting.
ipa: /ɛl nɛ pa vny a la ʁe.y.njɔ̃/
notes: Venue agrees in the feminine with elle, adding a silent e to the past participle.

fr: Nous ne sommes pas allés au cinéma dimanche.
en: We didn't go to the movies on Sunday.
ipa: /nu nə sɔm pa.z‿a.le o si.ne.ma di.mɑ̃ʃ/
notes: Allés takes the plural agreement s with nous even though the s is silent.

fr: Il n'est pas resté longtemps chez nous.
en: He didn't stay long at our place.
ipa: /il nɛ pa ʁɛs.te lɔ̃.tɑ̃ ʃe nu/
notes: Longtemps ends in a silent group of letters, so the nasal sound is your only clue to the spelling.

fr: Je ne suis pas arrivé à l'heure ce matin.
en: I didn't arrive on time this morning.
ipa: /ʒə nə sɥi pa a.ʁi.ve a lœʁ sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: À l'heure uses the preposition à, distinct from the verb a used elsewhere in similar sentences.

fr: Elle n'a pas acheté de pain hier.
en: She didn't buy any bread yesterday.
ipa: /ɛl na pa aʃ.te də pɛ̃ jɛʁ/
notes: After a negated verb, du pain becomes de pain, dropping the article entirely.

fr: Nous n'avons pas mangé au restaurant ce week-end.
en: We didn't eat at a restaurant this weekend.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ pa mɑ̃.ʒe o ʁɛs.to.ʁɑ̃ sə wik.ɛnd/
notes: The negation frames avons, so pas sits between the auxiliary and the past participle mangé.

fr: Ils ne sont pas partis en vacances cette année.
en: They didn't go on vacation this year.
ipa: /il nə sɔ̃ pa paʁ.ti ɑ̃ va.kɑ̃s sɛt a.ne/
notes: Partis carries a silent plural s agreeing with ils.

fr: Tu n'as pas appelé ta mère depuis lundi.
en: You haven't called your mother since Monday.
ipa: /ty na pa a.pə.le ta mɛʁ də.pɥi lœ̃.di/
notes: Appelé keeps a double p in spelling even though it sounds like a single consonant.

fr: Il n'a pas trouvé ses clés ce matin.
en: He didn't find his keys this morning.
ipa: /il na pa tʁu.ve se kle sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: Ses sounds identical to ces and c'est, so only the meaning tells you which spelling fits.

fr: Je n'ai pas dormi cette nuit.
en: I didn't sleep last night.
ipa: /ʒə nɛ pa dɔʁ.mi sɛt nɥi/
notes: Dormi keeps a regular participle ending with no silent letters, unlike many irregular verbs in this theme.

fr: Elle n'a pas pu venir à la fête.
en: She couldn't come to the party.
ipa: /ɛl na pa py və.niʁ a la fɛt/
notes: Pu is the short, irregular past participle of pouvoir and is easy to misspell as pue or pus.

fr: Nous n'avons pas eu de nouvelles depuis mardi.
en: We haven't had any news since Tuesday.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ pa y də nu.vɛl də.pɥi maʁ.di/
notes: Eu is pronounced with a single vowel sound but spelled with two letters, a common dictée trap.

fr: Vous n'êtes pas passés par la boulangerie.
en: You didn't go by the bakery.
ipa: /vu nɛt pa pa.se paʁ la bu.lɑ̃ʒ.ʁi/
notes: Êtes carries a circumflex accent that changes the sound of the e.

fr: Ils n'ont pas fini le projet à temps.
en: They didn't finish the project on time.
ipa: /il nɔ̃ pa fi.ni lə pʁɔ.ʒɛ a tɑ̃/
notes: Ont is easily confused with on, so listen to the sentence structure to choose the right spelling.

fr: Je n'ai pas encore lu ce livre.
en: I haven't read this book yet.
ipa: /ʒə nɛ pa ɑ̃.kɔʁ ly sə livʁ/
notes: Encore keeps its nasal en sound distinct from the verb ending in similar words.

fr: Elle n'a jamais visité Paris avant cette année.
en: She had never visited Paris before this year.
ipa: /ɛl na ʒa.mɛ vi.zi.te pa.ʁi a.vɑ̃ sɛt a.ne/
notes: Jamais replaces pas in this negation and must still surround the auxiliary a and the participle.

fr: Nous n'avons plus parlé depuis notre dispute.
en: We haven't spoken since our argument.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ ply paʁ.le də.pɥi nɔtʁ dis.pyt/
notes: Plus loses its final s sound in this negative meaning, unlike when it means more.

fr: Il n'a rien dit pendant toute la réunion.
en: He said nothing during the whole meeting.
ipa: /il na ʁjɛ̃ di pɑ̃.dɑ̃ tut la ʁe.y.njɔ̃/
notes: Rien slots between the auxiliary a and the past participle dit, unlike pas which surrounds it the same way.

fr: Tu n'as vu personne au bureau hier.
en: You didn't see anyone at the office yesterday.
ipa: /ty na vy pɛʁ.sɔn o by.ʁo jɛʁ/
notes: Personne here means nobody, not the noun for a person, so context decides the meaning.

fr: Je n'ai pas reçu ton colis.
en: I didn't receive your package.
ipa: /ʒə nɛ pa ʁə.sy tɔ̃ kɔ.li/
notes: Reçu needs a cedilla under the c to keep the soft s sound before u.

fr: Elle n'a pas signé le contrat.
en: She didn't sign the contract.
ipa: /ɛl na pa si.ɲe lə kɔ̃.tʁa/
notes: Signé uses gn to make the nasal palatal sound, a common spelling trap.

fr: Nous n'avons pas réservé de table.
en: We didn't reserve a table.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ pa ʁe.zɛʁ.ve də tabl/
notes: After the negation, une table becomes de table, dropping the indefinite article.

fr: Ils n'ont pas remarqué l'erreur.
en: They didn't notice the mistake.
ipa: /il nɔ̃ pa ʁə.maʁ.ke lɛ.ʁœʁ/
notes: L'erreur elides le before the vowel sound of erreur, and erreur itself doubles the r.

fr: Il n'a pas travaillé la semaine dernière.
en: He didn't work last week.
ipa: /il na pa tʁa.va.je la sə.mɛn dɛʁ.njɛʁ/
notes: Travaillé ends in a silent é sound spelled with the participle ending rather than an accented e alone.

fr: Je n'ai pas osé lui parler.
en: I didn't dare speak to him.
ipa: /ʒə nɛ pa o.ze lɥi paʁ.le/
notes: Osé and hier can sound alike in fast speech, so listen for the full word before writing.

fr: Elle n'a pas voulu sortir hier soir.
en: She didn't want to go out last night.
ipa: /ɛl na pa vu.ly sɔʁ.tiʁ jɛʁ swaʁ/
notes: Voulu is the irregular past participle of vouloir and does not follow the usual é ending pattern.

fr: Nous n'avons pas pu réparer la voiture.
en: We couldn't repair the car.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ pa py ʁe.pa.ʁe la vwa.tyʁ/
notes: Two verbs pu and réparer sit side by side, and only pu carries the negation.

fr: Vous n'avez pas oublié votre rendez-vous.
en: You didn't forget your appointment.
ipa: /vu na.ve pa u.bli.je vɔtʁ ʁɑ̃.de.vu/
notes: Rendez-vous keeps its hyphens and a silent z in rendez when spoken quickly.

fr: Je ne vais pas sortir ce soir.
en: I'm not going to go out tonight.
ipa: /ʒə nə vɛ pa sɔʁ.tiʁ sə swaʁ/
notes: In futur proche negation, pas surrounds vais, not the infinitive sortir.

fr: Elle ne va pas accepter cette offre.
en: She isn't going to accept this offer.
ipa: /ɛl nə va pa.z‿ak.sɛp.te sɛt ɔfʁ/
notes: Va links to accepter with a liaison z sound before the vowel a.

fr: Nous n'allons pas déménager cette année.
en: We aren't going to move this year.
ipa: /nu na.lɔ̃ pa de.me.na.ʒe sɛt a.ne/
notes: N'allons elides ne before the vowel of allons, so the apostrophe is required.

fr: Il ne va jamais oublier ce voyage.
en: He is never going to forget this trip.
ipa: /il nə va ʒa.mɛ u.bli.je sə vwa.jaʒ/
notes: Jamais replaces pas here but still comes right after the conjugated verb va.

fr: Tu ne vas plus travailler ici après juin.
en: You are no longer going to work here after June.
ipa: /ty nə va ply tʁa.va.je i.si a.pʁɛ ʒɥɛ̃/
notes: Plus drops its final s sound in this negative sense, unlike in comparisons.

fr: Ils ne vont pas venir à la fête.
en: They aren't going to come to the party.
ipa: /il nə vɔ̃ pa və.niʁ a la fɛt/
notes: Vont is easy to confuse with on or ont by sound, so check the subject ils carefully.

fr: Je ne vais rien changer dans mon emploi du temps.
en: I'm not going to change anything in my schedule.
ipa: /ʒə nə vɛ ʁjɛ̃ ʃɑ̃.ʒe dɑ̃ mɔ̃.n‿ɑ̃.plwa dy tɑ̃/
notes: Rien sits right after vais, framing the infinitive changer just like pas would.

fr: Elle ne va voir personne ce week-end.
en: She isn't going to see anyone this weekend.
ipa: /ɛl nə va vwaʁ pɛʁ.sɔn sə wik.ɛnd/
notes: Personne needs the double n even though French speakers often shorten it in speech.

fr: Nous n'allons acheter qu'un seul billet.
en: We are only going to buy one ticket.
ipa: /nu na.lɔ̃.z‿aʃ.te kœ̃ sœl bi.jɛ/
notes: Que elides to qu' before the vowel sound of un, marking the restriction only.

fr: Vous n'allez pas regretter cette décision.
en: You aren't going to regret this decision.
ipa: /vu na.le pa ʁə.ɡʁɛ.te sɛt de.si.zjɔ̃/
notes: N'allez elides ne before the vowel of allez, requiring the apostrophe in writing.

fr: Il ne va pas prendre le train demain.
en: He isn't going to take the train tomorrow.
ipa: /il nə va pa pʁɑ̃dʁ lə tʁɛ̃ də.mɛ̃/
notes: Train and demain both end in nasal vowels that can be hard to tell apart by ear.

fr: Je ne vais pas manger de viande ce soir.
en: I'm not going to eat meat tonight.
ipa: /ʒə nə vɛ pa mɑ̃.ʒe də vjɑ̃d sə swaʁ/
notes: After the negation, de la viande shortens to de viande, losing the article.

fr: Elle ne va pas répondre à cet email.
en: She isn't going to reply to this email.
ipa: /ɛl nə va pa ʁe.pɔ̃dʁ a sɛ.t‿i.mɛl/
notes: À cet uses a liaison t sound before email, distinct from writing a alone.

fr: Nous n'allons pas rester longtemps à la fête.
en: We aren't going to stay long at the party.
ipa: /nu na.lɔ̃ pa ʁɛs.te lɔ̃.tɑ̃ a la fɛt/
notes: Longtemps ends with silent letters after its nasal vowel sound.

fr: Tu ne vas pas aimer cette nouvelle règle.
en: You aren't going to like this new rule.
ipa: /ty nə va pa.z‿ɛ.me sɛt nu.vɛl ʁɛɡl/
notes: Vas links to aimer with a liaison z sound before the vowel.

fr: Ils ne vont plus habiter dans ce quartier.
en: They are no longer going to live in this neighborhood.
ipa: /il nə vɔ̃ ply.z‿a.bi.te dɑ̃ sə kaʁ.tje/
notes: The silent h in habiter still allows a liaison z sound from plus before it.

fr: Je ne vais jamais oublier ce moment.
en: I am never going to forget this moment.
ipa: /ʒə nə vɛ ʒa.mɛ u.bli.je sə mɔ.mɑ̃/
notes: Jamais keeps its final s silent, unlike when linked before a vowel.

fr: Elle ne va pas finir le rapport ce soir.
en: She isn't going to finish the report tonight.
ipa: /ɛl nə va pa fi.niʁ lə ʁa.pɔʁ sə swaʁ/
notes: Rapport doubles its p in spelling though it is pronounced as a single consonant.

fr: Nous n'allons pas prendre de dessert.
en: We aren't going to have dessert.
ipa: /nu na.lɔ̃ pa pʁɑ̃dʁ də de.sɛʁ/
notes: After the negation, du dessert becomes de dessert, dropping the partitive article.

fr: Il ne va pas conduire aujourd'hui.
en: He isn't going to drive today.
ipa: /il nə va pa kɔ̃.dɥiʁ o.ʒuʁ.dɥi/
notes: Conduire keeps a nasal on sound in its first syllable, distinct from the on of onze.

fr: Je ne bois que de l'eau le matin.
en: I only drink water in the morning.
ipa: /ʒə nə bwa kə də lo lə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: De l'eau elides twice in a row, and both apostrophes must appear in writing.

fr: Elle ne travaille que trois jours par semaine.
en: She only works three days a week.
ipa: /ɛl nə tʁa.vaj kə tʁwa ʒuʁ paʁ sə.mɛn/
notes: The unstressed que is often swallowed in fast speech but must still be written out.

fr: Nous ne mangeons que des produits frais.
en: We only eat fresh products.
ipa: /nu nə mɑ̃.ʒɔ̃ kə de pʁɔ.dɥi fʁɛ/
notes: Mangeons keeps the extra e before ons to preserve the soft g sound.

fr: Il ne parle que de son travail.
en: He only talks about his work.
ipa: /il nə paʁl kə də sɔ̃ tʁa.vaj/
notes: Que de son can blur together in speech, so listen for each separate word.

fr: Tu ne penses qu'à tes vacances.
en: You only think about your vacation.
ipa: /ty nə pɑ̃s ka te va.kɑ̃s/
notes: Que elides to qu' before à, and the two together sound like a single syllable.

fr: Je n'ai qu'une seule sœur.
en: I only have one sister.
ipa: /ʒə nɛ kyn sœl sœʁ/
notes: Qu'une elides que before the vowel of une, so the apostrophe cannot be dropped.

fr: Elle ne lit que des romans policiers.
en: She only reads detective novels.
ipa: /ɛl nə li kə de ʁɔ.mɑ̃ pɔ.li.sje/
notes: Policiers ends in a silent s that marks the plural agreement with romans.

fr: Nous n'avons que deux heures avant le train.
en: We only have two hours before the train.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ kə dø.z‿œʁ a.vɑ̃ lə tʁɛ̃/
notes: Deux heures links with a liaison z sound, and heures itself begins with a silent h.

fr: Il ne sort que le week-end.
en: He only goes out on weekends.
ipa: /il nə sɔʁ kə lə wik.ɛnd/
notes: Sort ends in a silent t that must still be written.

fr: Ils ne mangent que des légumes bio.
en: They only eat organic vegetables.
ipa: /il nə mɑ̃ʒ kə de le.ɡym bjo/
notes: Mangent keeps a silent ent ending that shows the plural ils, not a pronounced sound.

fr: Je ne connais que le centre-ville.
en: I only know the city center.
ipa: /ʒə nə kɔ.nɛ kə lə sɑ̃tʁ vil/
notes: Connais ends with a silent s, part of the irregular verb connaître.

fr: Elle n'écoute que de la musique classique.
en: She only listens to classical music.
ipa: /ɛl ne.kut kə də la my.zik kla.sik/
notes: N'écoute elides ne before the vowel of écoute, keeping the apostrophe in writing.

fr: Nous ne visitons que les grandes villes.
en: We only visit big cities.
ipa: /nu nə vi.zi.tɔ̃ kə le ɡʁɑ̃d vil/
notes: Grandes carries a silent final e and s marking feminine plural agreement with villes.

fr: Il ne prend que le bus le matin.
en: He only takes the bus in the morning.
ipa: /il nə pʁɑ̃ kə lə bys lə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: Prend ends in a silent d that is easy to forget when writing quickly.

fr: Tu ne portes que du noir en hiver.
en: You only wear black in winter.
ipa: /ty nə pɔʁt kə dy nwaʁ ɑ̃.n‿i.vɛʁ/
notes: En hiver links with a nasal liaison sound before the silent h of hiver.

fr: Je ne parle que français à la maison.
en: I only speak French at home.
ipa: /ʒə nə paʁl kə fʁɑ̃.sɛ a la mɛ.zɔ̃/
notes: Français needs its cedilla to keep the soft s sound before the a.

fr: Elle n'utilise que son téléphone pour travailler.
en: She only uses her phone to work.
ipa: /ɛl ny.ti.liz kə sɔ̃ te.le.fɔn puʁ tʁa.va.je/
notes: N'utilise elides ne before the vowel of utilise, so the apostrophe must appear.

fr: Nous n'avons qu'une seule voiture dans la famille.
en: We only have one car in the family.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ kyn sœl vwa.tyʁ dɑ̃ la fa.mij/
notes: Qu'une elides que before une, collapsing two words into one quick sound.

fr: Il ne dort que six heures par nuit.
en: He only sleeps six hours a night.
ipa: /il nə dɔʁ kə si.z‿œʁ paʁ nɥi/
notes: Six links to heures with a liaison z sound, changing the usual final consonant of six.

fr: Ils ne visitent que le musée le samedi.
en: They only visit the museum on Saturdays.
ipa: /il nə vi.zit kə lə my.ze lə sam.di/
notes: Visitent ends in a silent ent that marks the plural ils without an extra syllable.

fr: Je ne fume jamais en public.
en: I never smoke in public.
ipa: /ʒə nə fym ʒa.mɛ ɑ̃ py.blik/
notes: En public uses a nasal en sound rather than a pronounced n before public.

fr: Elle ne mange plus de sucre.
en: She no longer eats sugar.
ipa: /ɛl nə mɑ̃ʒ ply də sykʁ/
notes: Plus loses its final s sound in this negative meaning of no longer.

fr: Nous ne comprenons rien à ce problème.
en: We understand nothing about this problem.
ipa: /nu nə kɔ̃.pʁə.nɔ̃ ʁjɛ̃ a sə pʁɔ.blɛm/
notes: Rien à can blend together in speech, so listen for the separate preposition à.

fr: Il ne connaît personne dans cette ville.
en: He doesn't know anyone in this city.
ipa: /il nə kɔ.nɛ pɛʁ.sɔn dɑ̃ sɛt vil/
notes: Connaît carries a circumflex accent over the i that changes nothing in sound but is required in spelling.

fr: Tu n'as aucune excuse pour ton retard.
en: You have no excuse for your lateness.
ipa: /ty na o.kyn ɛk.skyz puʁ tɔ̃ ʁə.taʁ/
notes: Aucune agrees in the feminine with excuse, not the masculine aucun.

fr: Je ne bois ni café ni thé le soir.
en: I drink neither coffee nor tea in the evening.
ipa: /ʒə nə bwa ni ka.fe ni te lə swaʁ/
notes: Thé keeps a silent h after the t, a common spelling trap in this word.

fr: Elle ne sort jamais sans son sac.
en: She never goes out without her bag.
ipa: /ɛl nə sɔʁ ʒa.mɛ sɑ̃ sɔ̃ sak/
notes: Sans and son both use nasal vowels that can sound alike if you don't listen closely.

fr: Nous ne regardons plus la télévision le soir.
en: We no longer watch television in the evening.
ipa: /nu nə ʁə.ɡaʁ.dɔ̃ ply la te.le.vi.zjɔ̃ lə swaʁ/
notes: Plus drops its final s sound here, unlike when it means more of something.

fr: Il ne dit jamais la vérité sur son âge.
en: He never tells the truth about his age.
ipa: /il nə di ʒa.mɛ la ve.ʁi.te syʁ sɔ.n‿aʒ/
notes: Son âge links with a liaison n sound before the circumflex a of âge.

fr: Ils n'ont aucun problème avec ce plan.
en: They have no problem with this plan.
ipa: /il nɔ̃.t‿o.kœ̃ pʁɔ.blɛm a.vɛk sə plɑ̃/
notes: Ont links to aucun with a liaison t sound before the vowel.

fr: Je ne vois personne dans la rue ce matin.
en: I don't see anyone in the street this morning.
ipa: /ʒə nə vwa pɛʁ.sɔn dɑ̃ la ʁy sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: Personne keeps its double n in spelling despite the single nasal sound heard.

fr: Elle ne mange rien avant le sport.
en: She eats nothing before sports.
ipa: /ɛl nə mɑ̃ʒ ʁjɛ̃.n‿a.vɑ̃ lə spɔʁ/
notes: Rien links to avant with a liaison n sound before the vowel a.

fr: Nous ne voyageons jamais en hiver.
en: We never travel in winter.
ipa: /nu nə vwa.ja.ʒɔ̃ ʒa.mɛ ɑ̃.n‿i.vɛʁ/
notes: Voyageons keeps the extra e before ons to preserve the soft g sound.

fr: Il ne fait plus de sport depuis son accident.
en: He no longer plays sports since his accident.
ipa: /il nə fɛ ply də spɔʁ də.pɥi sɔ.n‿ak.si.dɑ̃/
notes: Son accident links with a liaison n sound before the vowel a.

fr: Tu ne réponds jamais à mes messages.
en: You never reply to my messages.
ipa: /ty nə ʁe.pɔ̃ ʒa.mɛ a me me.saʒ/
notes: Réponds ends in a silent d that comes from the verb répondre.

fr: Je n'ai aucune idée de l'heure qu'il est.
en: I have no idea what time it is.
ipa: /ʒə nɛ o.kyn i.de də lœʁ kil ɛ/
notes: Qu'il elides que before il, and the h of heure stays silent throughout the phrase.

fr: Elle ne conduit jamais la nuit.
en: She never drives at night.
ipa: /ɛl nə kɔ̃.dɥi ʒa.mɛ la nɥi/
notes: Conduit ends in a silent t that is part of the irregular verb conduire.

fr: Nous ne prenons plus le métro le soir.
en: We no longer take the metro in the evening.
ipa: /nu nə pʁə.nɔ̃ ply lə me.tʁo lə swaʁ/
notes: Plus is pronounced without its final s in this meaning of no longer.

fr: Il ne parle ni anglais ni espagnol.
en: He speaks neither English nor Spanish.
ipa: /il nə paʁl ni ɑ̃.ɡlɛ ni ɛs.pa.ɲɔl/
notes: Espagnol uses gn to make the nasal palatal sound, easy to misspell as ni or nj.

fr: Ils ne font rien pendant les vacances.
en: They do nothing during the holidays.
ipa: /il nə fɔ̃ ʁjɛ̃ pɑ̃.dɑ̃ le va.kɑ̃s/
notes: Font sounds close to fond, so listen to the verb ending rather than guessing from sound alone.

fr: Je ne connais aucun restaurant dans ce quartier.
en: I don't know any restaurant in this neighborhood.
ipa: /ʒə nə kɔ.nɛ o.kœ̃ ʁɛs.to.ʁɑ̃ dɑ̃ sə kaʁ.tje/
notes: Aucun is spelled with au, not o, even though the sound is short and simple.

fr: Elle n'invite jamais ses voisins.
en: She never invites her neighbors.
ipa: /ɛl nɛ̃.vit ʒa.mɛ se vwa.zɛ̃/
notes: N'invite elides ne before the vowel of invite, keeping the required apostrophe.

fr: Nous ne mangeons ni viande ni poisson.
en: We eat neither meat nor fish.
ipa: /nu nə mɑ̃.ʒɔ̃ ni vjɑ̃d ni pwa.sɔ̃/
notes: Poisson doubles its s to keep the sharp s sound rather than a z sound.

fr: Il ne trouve personne pour l'aider.
en: He finds nobody to help him.
ipa: /il nə tʁuv pɛʁ.sɔn puʁ lɛ.de/
notes: L'aider elides le before the vowel of aider, so the apostrophe cannot be skipped.

fr: Tu ne changes jamais d'avis.
en: You never change your mind.
ipa: /ty nə ʃɑ̃ʒ ʒa.mɛ da.vi/
notes: D'avis elides de before the vowel of avis, collapsing the two words in speech.

fr: Il n'a pas de temps à perdre aujourd'hui.
en: He has no time to waste today.
ipa: /il na pa də tɑ̃ a pɛʁdʁ o.ʒuʁ.dɥi/
notes: A and à sound identical, so only the grammar tells you the verb from the preposition.

fr: Elle n'a pas dit où elle allait.
en: She didn't say where she was going.
ipa: /ɛl na pa di u ɛl a.lɛ/
notes: Où takes a grave accent to distinguish it from ou meaning or.

fr: On ne sait jamais ce qui va arriver.
en: You never know what is going to happen.
ipa: /ɔ̃ nə sɛ ʒa.mɛ sə ki va a.ʁi.ve/
notes: On sounds exactly like ont, so check whether a subject or a verb is needed.

fr: Ils n'ont pas de voiture pour aller au travail.
en: They don't have a car to go to work.
ipa: /il nɔ̃ pa də vwa.tyʁ puʁ a.le o tʁa.vaj/
notes: Ont is the verb form here, not the subject pronoun on, though both sound the same.

fr: Elle n'a pas encore décidé où partir en vacances.
en: She hasn't decided yet where to go on vacation.
ipa: /ɛl na pa ɑ̃.kɔʁ de.si.de u paʁ.tiʁ ɑ̃ va.kɑ̃s/
notes: Où needs its accent to mean where, unlike the unaccented ou meaning or.

fr: On n'a pas terminé le rapport à temps.
en: We didn't finish the report on time.
ipa: /ɔ̃ na pa tɛʁ.mi.ne lə ʁa.pɔʁ a tɑ̃/
notes: On n'a combines two easily confused sounds, on with ont and a with à, in one short phrase.

fr: Il n'a pas répondu à sa lettre.
en: He didn't reply to her letter.
ipa: /il na pa ʁe.pɔ̃.dy a sa lɛtʁ/
notes: À sa lettre uses the preposition à, not the verb a used earlier in the sentence.

fr: Nous ne savons pas où se trouve la gare.
en: We don't know where the station is.
ipa: /nu nə sa.vɔ̃ pa u sə tʁuv la ɡaʁ/
notes: Où carries an accent to separate it from the conjunction ou meaning or.

fr: On ne mange jamais avant midi ici.
en: People never eat before noon here.
ipa: /ɔ̃ nə mɑ̃ʒ ʒa.mɛ a.vɑ̃ mi.di i.si/
notes: On is the subject pronoun here and should never be confused with the verb form ont.

fr: Ils n'ont plus rien à ajouter au dossier.
en: They have nothing more to add to the file.
ipa: /il nɔ̃ ply ʁjɛ̃.n‿a a.ʒu.te o dɔ.sje/
notes: Rien à links with a liaison n before the vowel a, and à itself is the preposition, not the verb a.

fr: Elle n'a aucune idée où sont ses clés.
en: She has no idea where her keys are.
ipa: /ɛl na o.kyn i.de u sɔ̃ se kle/
notes: Sont sounds like son but means are, so listen to the full sentence to tell them apart.

fr: On ne vend plus ce modèle en magasin.
en: This model is no longer sold in stores.
ipa: /ɔ̃ nə vɑ̃ ply sə mɔ.dɛl ɑ̃ ma.ɡa.zɛ̃/
notes: On here stands for people in general, distinct in spelling from the verb form ont.

fr: Il n'a pas voulu dire où il était allé.
en: He didn't want to say where he had gone.
ipa: /il na pa vu.ly diʁ u i.l‿e.tɛ a.le/
notes: Où keeps its accent for where, never to be confused with the plain ou meaning or.

fr: Nous n'avons pas su où garer la voiture.
en: We didn't know where to park the car.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ pa sy u ɡa.ʁe la vwa.tyʁ/
notes: Où needs its grave accent, unlike ou which links two choices together.

fr: On n'a jamais visité ce pays ensemble.
en: We have never visited this country together.
ipa: /ɔ̃ na ʒa.mɛ vi.zi.te sə pe.i ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl/
notes: On n'a combines the subject on, easily confused with ont, and the elided n'a.

fr: Elle n'a pas encore trouvé où habiter.
en: She hasn't found where to live yet.
ipa: /ɛl na pa ɑ̃.kɔʁ tʁu.ve u a.bi.te/
notes: Où needs its accent even though habiter begins with a silent h right after it.

fr: Ils n'ont aucune préférence pour le restaurant.
en: They have no preference for the restaurant.
ipa: /il nɔ̃.t‿o.kyn pʁe.fe.ʁɑ̃s puʁ lə ʁɛs.to.ʁɑ̃/
notes: Ont links to aucune with a liaison t sound, and aucune agrees in the feminine with préférence.

fr: Il n'a pas de raison de s'inquiéter.
en: He has no reason to worry.
ipa: /il na pa də ʁɛ.zɔ̃ də sɛ̃.kje.te/
notes: S'inquiéter elides se before the vowel of inquiéter, so the apostrophe must be written.

fr: On ne connaît personne à cette adresse.
en: Nobody knows anyone at this address.
ipa: /ɔ̃ nə kɔ.nɛ pɛʁ.sɔn a sɛt a.dʁɛs/
notes: On and à cette both hide easily confused homophones, on versus ont and à versus a.

fr: Nous n'avons pas vu où il est parti.
en: We didn't see where he went.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ pa vy u i.l‿ɛ paʁ.ti/
notes: Où takes its accent for where, distinct from the linking word ou.

fr: Elle n'a jamais su où était son père.
en: She never knew where her father was.
ipa: /ɛl na ʒa.mɛ sy u e.tɛ sɔ̃ pɛʁ/
notes: Où contrasts with the unaccented ou, and son here shows masculine agreement with père.

fr: On n'a plus de pain à la maison.
en: We don't have any bread left at home.
ipa: /ɔ̃ na ply də pɛ̃ a la mɛ.zɔ̃/
notes: On n'a plus combines the on and ont homophone trap with the silent s of plus.

fr: Il n'a que deux jours de congé ce mois-ci.
en: He only has two days off this month.
ipa: /il na kə dø ʒuʁ də kɔ̃.ʒe sə mwa.si/
notes: N'a que marks the restriction only, and que often gets swallowed into the surrounding sounds in fast speech.
